exposure: intrathecal midazolam (2 mg) with hyperbaric lidocaine
intrathecal tramadol (25 mg) with hyperbaric lidocaine
conventional method (hyperbaric lidocaine and normal saline (5 cc))
outcome: consumed dose of analgesics at 24 hours after surgery
cohort: 210 women aged 20-35 years with ASA class I and II who were candidates for elective cesarean section.
finding: Intrathecal tramadol significantly increased analgesia duration and reduced postoperative shivering and analgesic consumption compared to midazolam and control, with midazolam also demonstrating superior effects over control.
mod_finding: The study's findings demonstrate the effectiveness of intrathecal midazolam and tramadol in managing postoperative pain and shivering specifically following elective cesarean section.
